summary: Ferry County, WA 45-ft pole lookout built on Sheep Mountain in 1933-34, removed or destroyed in 1964; FFLOS-registered 2012; no current site description found.

facts.design: 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab and a 14 x 14-foot house on top
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1964; no source describes what remains on the site

events.note: Construction began: knocked-down station unloaded July 1933; tower raised by October 1933
Register and Firelookout date the lookout to 1934; crew of four under Glen Campbell completed the station in June 1934
Register and Forest Lookouts say removed; Firelookout and WillhiteWeb say destroyed
Registered November 19, 2012 as US 1464, WA 364; nominated by Ray Kresek

evidence.supports: about eight miles south-southwest of Republic, Ferry County
July 1933 station unloaded from cars for placement on the mountain
evidence.quote: In July 1933, men started unloading from cars a knocked-down lookout station to be placed on Sheep Mountain.

evidence.supports: by October tower raised and 14 x 14-foot house being built on top
evidence.quote: By October, the tower had been raised and a 14 x 14-foot house was being constructed on top of the tower.
Built in 1934, this 45' pole L-4 tower was removed in 1964.

evidence.supports: June 1934 crew of four under Glen Campbell completing station and installing lightning protection
evidence.quote: Glen Campbell has a crew of four men on Sheep mountain, completing the lookout station and installing lightning protection.

evidence.supports: June 1934 crew of four under Glen Campbell completing station and installing lightning protection
evidence.quote: The following year in June of 1934, the crew of four being led by Glen Campbell was completing the lookout station and installing lightning protection.

evidence.supports: 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
evidence.quote: The tower was a 45-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts lists the lookout as removed
administered by the U.S. Forest Service

corrections.why: Register, Firelookout and WillhiteWeb all describe a 45-foot pole tower (about 13.7 m); the 4.3 m figure matches no source read

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and Forest Lookouts say removed; Firelookout and WillhiteWeb say destroyed. All four agree on 1964. Story reports both words.
Register and Firelookout give 1934; newspaper-based pages show construction began in 1933 and was finished in 1934. Story gives both dates.

notes_for_editor: Gone site; no source describes what remains or whether the site is open, so facts.access is omitted (brief said unknown). No staffing, fire or NRHP record in the sources read. Brief height_m 4.3 proposed as 13.7 (45 ft). Register photos are not text, so none added. One WebSearch used; the second not needed.
